---
title: "A: Alimentary tract and metabolism"
description: "ATC group A covers the alimentary tract, also called the digestive or GI tract, and metabolism: from antacids and laxatives to diabetes drugs and vitamins."
date: "2026-02-08"
---

Drugs acting on the gut, on metabolism and on nutrition, from mouthwashes to insulins.

Insulin was first given to a patient in January 1922, at Toronto General Hospital.
The patient, Leonard Thompson, was 14 years old and seriously ill with diabetes.
The first injection of pancreatic extract lowered his blood glucose only slightly, had no effect on the buildup of acidic ketones in his blood (ketoacidosis) and left a collection of pus without infection (sterile abscess).
A second series of injections on 23 January brought his blood glucose down from 520 to 120 mg/dL and cleared the ketones from his urine.
Part of the credit goes to the biochemist James Collip, who had developed a new extraction and concentration protocol [@vecchioDiscoveryInsulinImportant2018].
